newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: TOP SLOVAK ACTORS TO STRIKE OVER GOVT INTERFERENCE.
newsitem.headline: TOP SLOVAK ACTORS TO STRIKE OVER GOVT INTERFERENCE.

text.p: The actors of Slovakia's prestigious National Theatre, the country's leading stage, said on Wednesday they would go on an indefinite strike to protest the sacking of their general director.

"There will be no public theatre performances as of Thursday," Ladislav Chudik, internationally respected doyen of Slovakia's acting community told a rally of some 10,000 people gathered in central Bratislava.

Wednesday's rally was held to protest Culture Minister Ivan Hudec's sacking of National Theatre General Director Dusan Jamrich, who was replaced by Miroslav Fischer, the current manager of the Chamber Opera.
"We shall continue to rehearse...but will not perform until proper competition is announced for the post of general director," Chudik said.

The only other time the National Theatre ever closed down was in November 1989 when the actors of all the stages in then-Czechoslovakia went on strike and held protest meetings which helpded spark the "Velvet Revolution" which brought downtr he communist government.

Hudec has further angered the country's intellectual community by sacking the chief of the Slovak Philharmonic. At least 35,000 people have signed a petition protesting against state interference in the autonomy of cultural institutions and calling for Hudec to resign.
